title: Why Clean Water Changes Everything
excerpt: A single borehole well can free up hours of a family's day and cut waterborne illness dramatically. Here's what we've learned from the Mwanza well project.
author: Amara Okafor
content: When we started the Mwanza well project, most families in the area spent up to three hours a day walking to and from the nearest water source.
Since the well opened, local health workers have reported a marked drop in waterborne illness among children under five.
Beyond health, the time saved has meant more children, especially girls, are able to stay in school.

title: Building With the Community, Not For It
excerpt: Every project starts with months of listening. Here's why we hire local labor and let communities lead the design process.
author: David Mensah
content: Before a single foundation is poured, our team spends weeks meeting with local leaders, teachers, and families to understand what's actually needed.
Every project hires local labor first, not only because it's more sustainable, but because it means the community has a direct hand in what gets built.
This approach takes longer, but the buildings that result are ones communities actually use and maintain long after we've left.

title: 2025 in Review: Five Projects, Three Countries
excerpt: A look back at what your donations helped build this year, from a new school in Nairobi to a clinic under construction in Lira.
author: Amara Okafor
content: This year, thanks to our donors, we broke ground on five projects across Kenya, Tanzania, and Uganda.
The Kibera Primary School opened its doors to 400 students, and the Lira Community Clinic is on track to open in early 2026.
Thank you to everyone who made this possible. None of this happens without your support.
